content:
You are revising a resume that has already been written for a candidate. Change as little as possible, and add no work the draft does not already describe.

THE DRAFT (its summary, and each role with its dates and bullets):
[[draftJson]]

TERMS THE RESUME IS MISSING. Each of these is on the target job's checklist and a scanner counts every one; the draft left them out:
[[missingTermsJson]]

[[figuresNote]]

WHAT TO DO

Put each missing term back, spelled EXACTLY as listed above - same words, same order, same singular or plural:
- into a bullet, only where that bullet already describes work that plainly involved it;
- otherwise into the summary, as part of what the candidate works with or knows ("services in Python and Kafka"), never as a claim about one particular piece of work.

A capability like "full-stack development" or "artificial intelligence" belongs inside a sentence about something that was built, never in a list and never as "experienced in", "familiar with" or "exposure to". A term you cannot place honestly in either way stays missing; a resume short of a keyword is a smaller problem than a line the candidate cannot defend. Return {} when nothing can honestly be changed.

Widen the sentences that are already there rather than adding new ones. A bullet may carry two or three of these terms and should still read as one thing that was done; 26-36 words is the room you have, and a role may not exceed 8 bullets.

THE YEARS RULE. A technology goes only into a bullet of a role whose dates it fits - nothing a role's years come before. One newer than every role goes in the summary, or stays missing.

THE INDUSTRY RULE. A term naming an INDUSTRY this candidate has not worked in - a clinical, legal, defence or trading practice on somebody whose draft shows no work in that field - stays out, whatever it would score.

WHAT MAY NOT CHANGE

Every employer, job title, date and location. Any project, client, system, technology, team, scale or outcome that is not already in the draft or among the missing terms: you are rewording what is there, not inventing more of it. Every figure already in a sentence stays exactly as written, and no figure is added except one the FIGURES lines above state, put back into the bullet about that same piece of work and nowhere else. Never a figure in the summary that the draft's summary does not already carry.

VOICE

Past tense, plain words, no em-dashes. Never these words in any form: leveraged, utilized, spearheaded, orchestrated, streamlined, seamless, robust, scalable, maximized, cross-functional, end-to-end, innovative, dynamic, cutting-edge, world-class, holistic, comprehensive, proven, strategic. Do not open a sentence with Designed, Architected, Led, Delivered, Drove, Integrated, Partnered, Supported, Contributed, Managed or Streamlined. Never let a bullet's verb repeat its own noun: "Automated model training workflow automation" is the shape to avoid.

RETURN

Only a JSON object, and only the parts you changed:

{
"summary": "the rewritten summary, or omit this key if you did not change it",
"experience": [
{ "company": "exactly as the draft spells it", "title": "exactly as the draft spells it", "achievements": ["every bullet for this role, in order, changed and unchanged alike"] }
]
}

List a role only if you changed one of its bullets, and when you do, return ALL of that role's bullets. Return nothing else: no skills, no cover letter, no dates, no commentary.
